professional [[basketball]] player for [[CB Canarias|La Laguna Tenerife]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]] as a [[shooting guard]] for three years and was named the [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|NCAA Tournament Most Outstanding Player]] during his junior season en route to winning the NCAA Championship. In high school, he was [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] and a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]]. ==Early years== [[File:20160330 MCDAAG Kyle Guy dribbling.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Guy during the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] Guy attended [[Lawrence Central High School]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]]. He was a varsity letter-winner all four years at Lawrence Central.{{cite web|url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/kyle_guy_1014830.html|title=Kyle Guy bio|work=VirginiaSports.com|access-date=November 23, 2016|archive-date=November 22, All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]].{{cite web|last1=Neddenriep|first1=Kyle|title=Guy, Corsaro and Young named McDonald's All American|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/01/17/guy-corsaro-and-young-named-mcdonalds-all-american/78951742/|website=IndyStar.com|access-date=November 23, 2016|date=January 18, 2016}} After averaging 23.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists during his senior season, he was selected as [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]].{{cite web|last1=Neddenriep|first1=Kyle|title=Kyle Guy of Lawrence Central wins Mr. Basketball|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/04/28/kyle-guy-lawrence-central-wins-mr-basketball/83677858/|website=IndyStar.com|access-date=November 23, 2016|date=April 29, 2016}} On October 20, 2014, Guy committed to playing college basketball at [[University of Virginia|Virginia]], selecting the Cavaliers over offers from schools such as [[University of California, Berkeley|California]], [[Xavier University|Xavier]], and [[Indiana University|Indiana]].{{cite web|last1=Wood|first1=Norm|title=ACC All Access: Highly-recruited guard Kyle Cavaliers Top VCU 76-67|url=http://www.nbc29.com/story/36874689/kyle-guy-scores-career-high-29-points-cavaliers-top-vcu-76-67|access-date=January 11, 2018|work=NBC 29|date=December 1, 2017|archive-date=January 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180112160143/http://www.nbc29.com/story/36874689/kyle-guy-scores-career-high-29-points-cavaliers-top-vcu-76-67|url-status=dead}} He had 22 points, including five three-pointers, in a 76–67 victory over [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] on January 10, 2018.{{cite news|title=Kyle Guy pushes No. 3 Virginia past Syracuse|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/01/09/guys-22-points-push-no-3-virginia-past-syracuse-68-61/109314638/|access-date=January 11, 2018|work=[[USA Today]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 10, 2018}} In the [[2018 ACC men's basketball tournament|2018 ACC tournament]], he led [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] to a conference tournament championship, where he averaged 16.7 points per game, earning him tournament MVP honors. Prior to the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]], Guy was named to the pre-season watchlists for the [[Jerry West Award]], [[John R. Wooden Award]], and [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Counts |first1=Ron |title=Virginia's Kyle Guy named to 2019 Jerry West Award watch list |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/virginia-s-kyle-guy-named-to-jerry-west-award-watch/article_92e89eaf-f82e-59cc-867c-04b65e391209.html |website=dailyprogress.com |access-date=November 12, 2018 |date=October 16, 2018}}{{cite web |title=Citizen Naismith Trophy Men's Watch List Released |url=http://naismithtrophy.com/citizen-naismith-trophy-mens-watch-list-released/ |website=naismithtrophy.com |access-date=November 12, 2018 |date=November 5, 2018}}{{cite web |title=JOHN R. WOODEN AWARD PRESENTED BY WENDY'S ANNOUNCES 2018-19 PRESEASON TOP 50 WATCH LIST |url=http://www.woodenaward.com/john_r_wooden_award_presented_by_wendy_s_announces_2018_19_preseason_top_50_watch_list |website=woodenaward.com |access-date=November 12, 2018 |date=November 6, 2018}} Guy set a new career high with 30 points against [[2018–19 Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball team|Marshall]] on December 31, 2018. He recorded his first collegiate double-double with 25 points and 10 rebounds on March 30, 2019, against [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] in the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]], helping the Cavaliers advance to the program's first Final Four since 1984 in the process.{{cite web |last1=Counts |first1=Ron |title=After pep talk from Kyle Guy, left after being fouled on a corner 3 to help the Cavaliers reach their first-ever national championship game.{{cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2019-04-06/virginia-auburn-score-kyle-guy-free-throws-send-cavaliers|title=Kyle Guy's free throws with 0.6 seconds remaining send Virginia to Men's Basketball Championship Game|championship game]], and was named the tournament's [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]].{{cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2019-final-four-all-tournament-team-kyle-guy-named-most-outstanding-player/ |title=2019 Final Four All-Tournament Team: Kyle Guy named Most Outstanding Player |publisher=CBSSports.com |date=April 8, 2019 |access-date=April 8, 2019|first=Chip|last=Patterson}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2019–2021)=== Guy was drafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[New York Knicks]] before being traded to Sacramento.{{cite web|title=Knicks Acquire Draft Rights to Ignas Brazdeikis|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-acquire-draft-rights-ignas-brazdeikis|date=June 20, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 21, 2019}} The Kings signed him to a [[two-way contract]] on July 7, 2019, to split time between the NBA Kings and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Stockton Kings]].{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Kyle Guy to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-kyle-guy-two-way-contract|date=July 7, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 7, 2019}} He scored 42 points for Stockton in a win over the [[Iowa Wolves]] on December 1.{{cite news|title=Kings' Kyle Guy: Explodes for 42 points Saturday|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-kyle-guy-explodes-for-42-points-saturday/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=December 1, 2019|access-date=January 11, 2020}} Guy made his NBA debut on January 10, 2020, against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite news|first=Sanjesh|last=Singh|title=Bucks 127, Kings 106: Slowed down Giannis, but not the rest of the herd|url=https://www.sactownroyalty.com/2020/1/10/21061033/bucks-127-kings-106-slowed-down-giannis-but-not-the-rest-of-the-herd|work=SacTown Royalty|date=January 10, 2020|access-date=January 11, 2020}} On January 18, he scored 37 points and hit seven three-pointers for Stockton in a 147–117 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite news|first=Cody|last=Taylor|title=Kings' Kyle Guy dropped 37 points in the G League on Friday night|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2020/01/18/kyle-guy-g-league-stats-stockton-kings-highlights-okc-blue/|work=Rookie Wire|date=January 18, 2020|access-date=January 21, 2020}} On March 25, 2021, Guy scored 17 points in 22 minutes off the bench for the [[Sacramento Kings]] in a 141–119 victory over the [[Golden State Warriors]] on 6-for-9 shooting, including 4-for-6 on [[three-point field goal]]s.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202103250SAC.html Box Score: Golden State Warriors at Sacramento Kings]. [[Basketball-Reference]], March 25, 2021. Accessed July 2, 2024. ===Cleveland Charge (2021)=== In August 2021, Guy joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{cite web|title=Warriors Announce Updated 2021 Summer League Roster, Presented by Oracle|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/summer-league-roster-20210807|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 10, 2021}} He debuted with 15 points in 17 minutes off the bench while 4-for-10 from the field, as well as 3-for-7 from three-point range against the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|title=Orlando vs. Golden State - Box Score - August 9, 2021 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba-summer/boxscore/_/gameId/401352146|website=ESPN.com|access-date=August 10, 2021}} On September 27, 2021, he signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]],{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Add Four to Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/21-22-camp-roster-210927|website=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2021|access-date=September 28, 2021}} but was waived on October 16.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Convert the Contracts of Tacko Fall and RJ Nembhard into Two-way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavaliers-convert-contracts-tacko-fall-and-rj-nembhard-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On October 23, he signed with the [[Cleveland Charge]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} ===Miami Heat (2021–2022)=== On December 30, 2021, Guy signed a 10-day contract with the [[Miami Heat]] via the hardship exemption.{{cite web|title=Heat Sign Kyle Guy And Aric Holman|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-kyle-guy-and-aric-holman|website=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2021|access-date=December 31, 2021}} In his first game after signing the 10-day contract, he scored 17 points in 23 minutes off the bench in a 120–110 victory over the [[Houston Rockets]] on 6-for-8 shooting, including 4-for-6 on [[three-point field goal]]s.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202112310HOU.html Box Score: Sacramento Kings at Houston Rockets]. [[Basketball-Reference]], December 31, 2021. Accessed July 2, 2024. He signed a second 10-day contract on January 10, 2022,{{cite web|title=HEAT RE-SIGN KYLE GUY AND CHRIS SILVA|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-kyle-guy-chris-silva|website=NBA.com|date=January 10, 2022|access-date=January 10, 2022}} then a full two-way contract with the Heat on January 17.{{cite web|title=(1) Miami HEAT on Twitter: "OFFICIAL: The Miami HEAT have signed Kyle Guy to a two-way contract.|url=https://twitter.com/MiamiHEAT/status/1483136532617830409|website=Twitter|date=January 17, 2022|access-date=January 17, 2022}} On March 24, he was waived by the Heat.{{cite web|title=Heat sign Mychal Mulder to 10-day contract, waive Kyle Guy|url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/heat-sign-mychal-mulder-to-10-day-contract-waive-kyle-guy/|website=HoopsHype.com|date=March 24, 2022|access-date=March 24, 2022|archive-date=July 15, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715100926/https://hoopshype.com/rumor/heat-sign-mychal-mulder-to-10-day-contract-waive-kyle-guy/|url-status=dead}} ===Return to the Charge (2022)=== On March 28, 2022, Guy returned to the [[Cleveland Charge]].{{cite web|title=Kyle Guy Returns to Charge|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/kyle-guy-returns-to-charge/|website=NBA.com|date=March 28, 2022|access-date=March 29, 2022}} ===Joventut Badalona (2022–2023)=== On July 22, 2022, Guy signed with Spanish club [[Joventut Badalona]]. In 21 [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] games, he averaged 11.8 points, 1.8 rebounds and 2.6 assists in 22 minutes per contest. Additionally, in 40 [[Liga ACB]] matches, he averaged 12.8 points, 1.8 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 23 minutes per contest. ===Panathinaikos (2023)=== In the 2023 offseason, Guy was initially approached by Spanish club [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]], which made him an official contract offer that was subsequently matched right at the deadline by [[Joventut Badalona]], under the Spanish basketball federation ''tanteo'' rule. On July 14, 2023, his contract was bought out by the Greek powerhouse [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], moving Guy to the [[EuroLeague]] for the first time in his career on a two-year deal.{{cite web|title=Kyle Guy In Green|url=https://www.paobc.gr/en/press-releases/103995_kyle-guy-green|website=paobc.gr|date=July 14, 2023|access-date=July 14, 2023}} ===La Laguna Tenerife (2024)=== On January 1, 2024, Guy signed with [[CB Canarias|Lenovo Tenerife]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-199627-kyle-guy-officially-leaves-panathinaikos-signs-a-deal-in-spain.html|title=Kyle Guy officially leaves Panathinaikos, signs a deal in Spain|last=|first=|date=January 1, 2024|website=|publisher=basketnews|language=En|access-date=April 28, 2024}} In the first round of the playoffs on May 18, he led all scorers with 34 points in a 96–86 losing effort at [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]]."[https://www.eldiario.es/canariasahora/deportes/baloncesto/barca-neutraliza-exhibicion-guy-gana-lenovo-primer-asalto_1_11378782.html Barça neutralizes Guy's display and beats Lenovo in the first round]". ''Deportes Canarias Ahora'', May 19, 2024. Accessed July 2, 2024. On August 7, Guy announced his transition to the "next chapter of [his] life" in a press release detailing his hiring as an assistant at [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|University of Virginia]].{{Cite web |date=2024-08-07 |title=Kyle Guy Returns to Grounds as Athlete Development Mentor/Special Assistant |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2024/08/07/kyle-guy-returns-to-grounds-as-athlete-development-mentor-special-assistant/ |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=Virginia Cavaliers Official Athletic Site |language=en-US}} ===Noblesville Boom (2025–2026)=== On October 18, 2025, Guy signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]] to play for their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Noblesville Boom]].{{cite web |title=Pacers Transactions - Oct. 18, 2025 |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-transactions-oct-18-2025 |website=NBA.com |access-date=18 October 2025}} On January 15, 2026, Guy was released by the Boom after a contract buyout, allowing him to play in China.{{cite news |last1=Dopirak |first1=Dustin |title=Lawrence Central's Kyle Guy released by Boom to pursue overseas offer |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2026/01/15/kyle-guy-of-lawrence-central-released-by-boom-to-pursue-overseas-offer/88200620007/ |access-date=15 January 2026 |work=Indianapolis Star |date=15 January 2026}}{{cite web |last1=Agness |first1=Scott |title=Kyle Guy departs Noblesville Boom after contract buyout |url=https://www.fieldhousefiles.com/p/kyle-guy-departs-noblesville-boom-contract-buyout |website=Fieldhouse Files with Scott Agness |access-date=15 January 2026}} ===Return to La Laguna Tenerife (2026–present)=== On July 13, 2026, Guy signed a two-year deal with [[CB Canarias|La Laguna Tenerife]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/news/tenerife-brings-back-sharp-shooter-kyle-guy/|title=Tenerife brings back sharp shooter Kyle Guy|date=July 13, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=July 13, 2026}} ==Coaching career== On August 7, 2024, Guy returned to his ''alma mater'' [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] to serve as the athlete development mentor/special assistant under head coach [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]].{{cite news|title=Kyle Guy Returns to Grounds as Athlete Development Mentor/Special Assistant|url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2024/08/07/kyle-guy-returns-to-grounds-as-athlete-development-mentor-special-assistant/|website=VirginiaSports.com|date=August 7, 2024|access-date=August 7, 2024}} In October 2024, after Bennett's surprising retirement, [[Ron Sanchez]] was promoted to interim head coach, and Guy served under him for the [[2024–25 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2024–25 season]]. In the spring of 2025, after a disappointing season, [[University of Virginia|Virginia]] [[Athletic director|AD]] [[Carla Williams (athletic director)|Carla Williams]] announced that Sanchez would not be retained with the hiring of [[Ryan Odom]].{{cite news | last = Newton | first = Matt | date = March 12, 2025 | title = Virginia Will Not Retain Ron Sanchez as Head Coach, Carla Williams Announces | url = https://www.si.com/college/virginia/virginia-will-not-retain-ron-sanchez-as-head-coach-carla-williams-announces | work = [[Sports Illustrated]] | access-date = 2025-05-14 }} Subsequently, Guy departed from the program to "pursue a new coaching opportunity". {{cite news | last = Chris | first = Graham | date = April 7, 2025 | title = Odom’s first flub as the UVA Basketball coach: Not retaining Kyle Guy | url = https://augustafreepress.com/news/odoms-first-flub-as-the-uva-basketball-coach-not-retaining-kyle-guy/ | work = [[Augusta Free Press]] | access-date = 2025-05-14 }} On April 11, 2025, [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]] announced Guy's hiring as an assistant coach under fellow Indiana native, [[Steve Alford]].{{Cite web |date=April 11, 2025 |title=Nevada Men’s Basketball Welcomes NCAA Champion and NBA Veteran Kyle Guy to Coaching Staff |url=https://nevadawolfpack.com/news/2025/4/11/mens-basketball-nevada-mens-basketball-welcomes-ncaa-champion-and-nba-veteran-kyle-guy-to-coaching-staff.aspx |access-date=April 22, 2025
